definition: A disturbance that transfers energy from place to place by oscillations, with no net transfer of matter.
A wave in which the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer, such as a wave on a rope or any electromagnetic wave.
A wave in which the oscillations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer, forming compressions and rarefactions, such as sound.
The distance between two neighbouring points on a wave that are in phase, such as one crest and the next; symbol $\lambda$, unit m.
A transverse wave of oscillating electric and magnetic fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel, that needs no medium and crosses a vacuum at speed $c$.

The whole range of electromagnetic waves, from gamma rays (shortest wavelength) through X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared and microwaves to radio waves (longest), all with the same speed in a vacuum.
The speed of every electromagnetic wave in a vacuum, $c = 3.00 \times 10^{8}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$; it is the same for all inertial observers.
